name: Flat Dumbbell Fly
nameDa: Flyes med håndvægte på flad bænk
grip: Neutral, palms facing each other, with wrists straight throughout the arc.
description: Open and close the arms in a broad arc above a flat bench while keeping a small, nearly fixed elbow bend.
setup: Sit with light dumbbells near the thighs and lie back with the weights controlled close to the chest.
Plant the feet and support the head, upper back and hips on the flat bench.
Bring the dumbbells above the chest with palms facing and elbows slightly bent.
instructions: Open the arms slowly out to the sides while preserving the elbow bend.
Stop around torso level, or earlier if needed to keep the shoulders comfortable.
Bring the arms together in the same arc above the chest.
Keep the dumbbells separate and lower them under control when ending the set.
commonMistakes: Changing elbow bend so the movement becomes a press.
Lowering too far or dropping the weights quickly into the stretched position.

logging.example: Two 12 kg dumbbells: record 12 kg per dumbbell.
logging.note: Keep the same exercise variant and record each dumbbell's mass rather than the combined pair.

variantNote: Flat bench with a neutral grip and nearly fixed elbow bend. Incline and decline fly variations are separate.
reviewNotes: Dumbbell fly depth must suit the individual; the drawing is not a depth prescription.
Trainer review of shoulder and elbow position pending.

sources.title: Muscle & Strength - Dumbbell Flys
sources.scope: Flat-bench fly, neutral hand position, controlled shoulder arc and consistent elbow bend.
